# JohnB.io

> A personal AI and development project site by John Bowman. Built to test, explore and showcase 28 free AI-powered tools, a 35-lesson AI & machine learning course across 9 units, responsible AI governance frameworks, and 212 iGaming compliance regulations across 50 jurisdictions.

Every public URL on JohnB.io serves clean Markdown for LLMs, answer engines, and automated crawlers via HTTP content negotiation (`Accept: text/markdown`, RFC 7763) or by appending `.md` to the canonical path (for example `https://johnb.io/index.md`, `https://johnb.io/aitocv.md`, `https://johnb.io/news/ai-models-2026.md`, `https://johnb.io/course/what-is-ai.md`). For a single-file concatenated Markdown bundle of the entire site, fetch [llms-full.txt](https://johnb.io/llms-full.txt).

- **Owner**: John Bowman (https://johnb.io/about) - AI strategist and developer based in Leeds, UK (20+ years in iGaming and digital marketing, University of Oxford AI Programme 2024).
- **Coverage**: 28 free browser & AI tools, 4 in-depth AI research articles, 35 free AI course lessons, and 212 iGaming regulations across 50 jurisdictions.
- **Stack & AI Models**: Vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript, Cloudflare Workers, Python (Pyodide), Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5), OpenAI (TTS-1 and GPT), and Google Gemini APIs.
- **Privacy & Disclosures**: All tools are free with no sign-up required. Tool inputs are processed ephemerally via Cloudflare Workers and never logged or stored. Contact and UK GDPR requests are handled via https://johnb.io/contact.

## Core Pages

- [Home](https://johnb.io/): A personal AI and development project site by John Bowman featuring 28 free AI-powered tools, a 35-lesson AI & machine learning course, responsible AI frameworks, and iGaming compliance utilities.
- [About John Bowman](https://johnb.io/about): John Bowman, AI strategist and developer based in Leeds, UK with 20+ years in iGaming and digital marketing, University of Oxford AI Programme graduate (2024), and creator of the free AI tools on JohnB.io.
- [AI & Machine Learning Course](https://johnb.io/course/): Free 9-unit, 35-lesson AI and machine learning course with certificate covering AI fundamentals, ethics, Python, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, MLOps and business strategy.
- [News and Insights](https://johnb.io/news/): Practical articles and analysis on AI models, generative engine optimisation (GEO), AI coding tools and digital strategy by John Bowman.

## AI Tools

- [Search & Prompt Radar](https://johnb.io/search-radar): Free keyword and prompt research tool that pulls live autocomplete suggestions from Google Search and YouTube, Reddit search intent, recent Hacker News threads and LinkedIn B2B modifiers, then synthesises likely ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude prompts using Claude Haiku 5.5.
- [AI Meditation Generator](https://johnb.io/meditation): Generates personalised guided meditations with Claude Sonnet 5.5 scripts, OpenAI TTS narration, and 10 browser-synthesised Web Audio soundscapes in 25 languages across 5, 10 or 20-minute sessions.
- [Live Poker Hand Replayer](https://johnb.io/live-poker-hand-replayer): Turn any live No Limit Hold'em poker hand into an animated table replay using a guided form or AI note parser powered by Claude Haiku 5.5, with optional OpenAI TTS commentary, share links and iframe embeds.
- [AI CV Enhancer](https://johnb.io/aitocv): Upload a CV (PDF, DOCX or TXT) and job description to get a tailored CV, cover letter, suitability match score and interview prep powered by Claude Sonnet 5.5 in 9 language variants, plus integrated job board search.
- [AI Copyeditor](https://johnb.io/editor): Paste or upload text and Word documents for AI-powered copyediting powered by Claude Sonnet 5.5 with UK/US English support, custom brand style guide rules and excluded words.
- [Gen Z Translator](https://johnb.io/genz): AI-powered translator using Claude Haiku 5.5 that rewrites plain English into Gen Z slang and translates Gen Z slang back into plain English.
- [LLM Chat](https://johnb.io/lm-chat): Side-by-side chat interface comparing Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT and Google Gemini responses to the same prompt in real time.
- [YouTube Blog Post Generator](https://johnb.io/transcripts): Paste a YouTube video URL or transcript and get a structured, SEO-optimised blog post generated by Claude Haiku 5.5.
- [Text to Speech Converter](https://johnb.io/text-to-speech): Convert text up to 4,000 characters to natural-sounding speech and download as MP3 using OpenAI TTS (tts-1) with six voices and adjustable speed.
- [Football 2026](https://johnb.io/football-2026): AI predictions for the Summer 2026 football tournament covering group stage results, interactive knockout bracket, squad ratings and win probabilities for all 48 teams.
- [Recipe to Shopping List](https://johnb.io/recipe-shopping-list): Paste a recipe or weekly meal plan to get one consolidated UK supermarket shopping list powered by Claude Haiku 5.5, grouped by aisle with US-to-UK ingredient translation and search links for Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Morrisons, Ocado, Waitrose, Iceland and Co-op.

## Developer Tools & iGaming Compliance

- [iGaming Bonus Cost Calculator](https://johnb.io/bonus-calculator): Model the true operator cost of casino bonus offers from bonus amount, wagering requirement, house edge and player completion rate, with breakeven analysis and scenario tables.
- [iGaming RG Message Generator](https://johnb.io/rg-generator): Generate compliant responsible gambling disclaimers for 10 regulated jurisdictions including UK (UKGC), Malta (MGA), Ontario, Netherlands, Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Ireland, Spain and Gibraltar.
- [iGaming Regulatory Compliance Map](https://johnb.io/igaming-compliance): Interactive world map and CC BY 4.0 dataset of 212 iGaming regulations across 50 jurisdictions covering gambling laws, AML directives, data protection rules and advertising codes.
- [iGaming Regulations Dataset (JSON)](https://johnb.io/igaming-regulations.json): Machine-readable CC BY 4.0 export of all 212 iGaming regulations across 50 jurisdictions with official regulator source links.
- [PDF Merger](https://johnb.io/pdf-merger): Merge multiple PDF files into one document directly in the browser using pdf-lib with drag-and-drop reordering and zero server uploads.
- [eBay & Vinted Profit Calculator](https://johnb.io/ebay): Calculate net profit and ROI from eBay, Vinted and auction saleroom sales after platform fees, buyer premiums, postage and purchase costs.
- [Bill Calculator](https://johnb.io/calculator): Split restaurant bills and calculate tips per person in the browser using Python running client-side via Pyodide.
- [Poker Bankroll Planner](https://johnb.io/bankroll): Evaluate poker experience level, session time and budget to plan a recommended game format, stake level and bankroll strategy.
- [Text to Voice](https://johnb.io/text-to-voice): Browser-based text-to-speech reader using the Web Speech API with voice selection, speed control and live word-by-word subtitle highlighting.

## Digital AI Tools

- [T&Cs Simplifier](https://johnb.io/tcs-simplifier): Paste casino bonus terms and conditions to get a plain English summary, red flag list and key numbers block (wagering, expiry, max bet, max win) powered by Claude Haiku 5.5.
- [Prompt Improver](https://johnb.io/prompt-improver): Rewrites weak AI prompts into stronger versions with a short change log using Claude Haiku 5.5, plus a starter library for common tasks across ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.
- [FAQ Schema Generator](https://johnb.io/faq-schema): Turns question and answer pairs into valid FAQPage JSON-LD structured data with a manual builder and an AI draft mode powered by Claude Haiku 5.5.
- [Content Repurposer](https://johnb.io/content-repurposer): AI-powered tool using Claude Haiku 5.5 that repurposes blog posts or articles into LinkedIn posts, X threads, Facebook posts, email newsletters and 10s/30s video scripts.
- [iGaming Promo Copy Generator](https://johnb.io/promo-copy): Generate compliant iGaming promotional copy for 10 regulated markets using Claude Haiku 5.5 with headlines, body copy, CTAs, T&C summaries and market-specific disclaimers.
- [iGaming Jargon Translator](https://johnb.io/igaming-jargon): AI-powered tool using Claude Haiku 5.5 that translates iGaming industry terminology (GGR, NGR, RTP, KYC/AML, CPA, RevShare) to plain English and vice versa.
- [LLMs.txt Generator](https://johnb.io/llms-generator): AI-powered tool using Claude Haiku 5.5 that generates a structured llms.txt file from a URL or pasted content following the llmstxt.org specification.

## Responsible AI

- [RAI Governance Framework](https://johnb.io/rai): Interactive browser-based responsible AI governance toolkit covering principles, EU AI Act risk tiering, RACI responsibility matrices, pre-deployment checklists, system cards and an AI system registry.

## News and Insights

- [News Index](https://johnb.io/news/): Practical articles and analysis on AI models, generative engine optimisation (GEO), AI coding tools and digital strategy by John Bowman.
- [AI Models in 2026: What Actually Changed in the Last 12 Months](https://johnb.io/news/ai-models-2026): A sourced review of AI progress from August 2025 to August 2026 covering Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5.5, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 and the Sora shutdown, Google Gemini 3, open-weight models, and the METR developer productivity trial.
- [What Happens When Your AI Songs Get 88 Million Views](https://johnb.io/news/ai-music-88-million-views): How John Bowman generated 88 million streams with AI music in 2024-2026, why it paid £600 in total, and how short-form video reach differs from streaming royalties.
- [GEO: A Practical Guide to Generative Engine Optimisation in 2026](https://johnb.io/news/geo-generative-engine-optimisation): Explains what Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) is, how it differs from traditional SEO, what AI retrieval systems extract, whether llms.txt works, and practical steps to earn citations in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews.
- [Claude Code VSC: AI Coding for Beginners](https://johnb.io/news/claude-code-vsc): Beginner's guide to Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension covering installation, CLAUDE.md project briefings, pricing (Claude Max vs API credits), and practical first workflows.

## AI & Machine Learning Course

- [AI & Machine Learning Course Hub](https://johnb.io/course/): Free 9-unit, 35-lesson AI and machine learning course with certificate covering AI fundamentals, ethics, Python, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, MLOps and business strategy.

### Unit 1 - Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
- [What is AI? - History, definitions & the Turing Test](https://johnb.io/course/what-is-ai): Covers AI history from the 1950s Dartmouth Workshop, Alan Turing's 1950 test, AI winters, and why modern AI is pattern matching at scale.
- [Categories of AI - Narrow, General & Super AI](https://johnb.io/course/categories-of-ai): Explains the three tiers of AI capability: Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI), Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), and Artificial Superintelligence (ASI).
- [How AI Learns - Supervised, Unsupervised & Reinforcement Learning](https://johnb.io/course/how-ai-learns): The three core learning paradigms that power modern AI systems, with practical examples of labelled training, clustering and reward-driven agents.
- [AI vs. Augmented Intelligence](https://johnb.io/course/ai-vs-augmented-intelligence): Explores the practical distinction between autonomous AI replacing human tasks and augmented intelligence enhancing human judgment.

### Unit 2 - The Modern AI Landscape
- [Traditional AI vs. Generative AI - Architecture differences](https://johnb.io/course/traditional-vs-generative-ai): How rules-based and predictive statistical AI differs from modern generative foundation models that synthesise text, code, audio and images.
- [Machine Learning, Deep Learning & Neural Networks - How they relate](https://johnb.io/course/ml-deep-learning-neural-networks): How classical machine learning, multi-layer neural networks and deep learning fit together and when simpler models outperform deep networks.
- [Key AI Subfields - NLP, Computer Vision & Edge AI](https://johnb.io/course/key-ai-subfields): Overview of natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, speech recognition, robotics and recommender systems.
- [AI Tools & Platforms - LLMs, Agents, RAG & the 2026 market](https://johnb.io/course/ai-tools-platforms-2026): Survey of the leading foundation models, APIs, cloud ML platforms and developer tools used in production in 2026.

### Unit 3 - Ethics, Governance & Responsible AI
- [Real-World AI Failures & Why Ethics Matter](https://johnb.io/course/ai-failures-ethics): Real-world case studies of AI deployment failures and the ethical governance principles needed to prevent harm.
- [Hallucinations, Bias & Intellectual Property](https://johnb.io/course/ai-hallucinations-bias-ip): Why large language models hallucinate, how training data bias propagates into decisions, and copyright and intellectual property considerations.
- [AI Governance Frameworks & Enterprise Guidelines](https://johnb.io/course/ai-governance-frameworks): How organisations and regulators govern AI systems under the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and UK AI principles.

### Unit 4 - Python for AI
- [Python Essentials for AI - Variables, data structures & control flow](https://johnb.io/course/python-essentials-for-ai): Core Python data structures, functions, comprehensions and environment management required for machine learning workflows.
- [Data Analysis with NumPy & Pandas](https://johnb.io/course/numpy-pandas): Vectorised array operations in NumPy and tabular data cleaning, filtering and aggregation with Pandas.

### Unit 5 - Machine Learning
- [Linear Regression & Gradient Descent](https://johnb.io/course/linear-regression-gradient-descent): How linear regression models continuous outcomes and how gradient descent iteratively minimises a loss function.
- [Logistic Regression & Classification](https://johnb.io/course/logistic-regression-classification): Binary and multi-class classification using the sigmoid function, log-loss optimisation and decision thresholds.
- [Model Evaluation - Validation, Overfitting & Metrics](https://johnb.io/course/model-evaluation): Measuring model performance with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, ROC-AUC and cross-validation.
- [Key ML Algorithms - Decision Trees, SVMs & More](https://johnb.io/course/key-ml-algorithms): Decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, support vector machines (SVMs) and k-nearest neighbours compared.

### Unit 6 - Deep Learning & Neural Networks
- [Biological vs. Artificial Neurons](https://johnb.io/course/biological-vs-artificial-neurons): How biological neurons inspired the mathematical perceptron, weights, biases and activation thresholds.
- [Artificial Neural Networks & Forward Propagation](https://johnb.io/course/neural-networks-forward-propagation): How input features flow through input, hidden and output layers via matrix multiplication and non-linear activations.
- [Backpropagation & How Neural Networks Learn](https://johnb.io/course/backpropagation): How neural networks learn by applying the chain rule of calculus to propagate error gradients backward through layers.
- [Activation Functions & the Vanishing Gradient Problem](https://johnb.io/course/activation-functions-vanishing-gradient): ReLU, sigmoid, tanh and softmax compared, and how vanishing or exploding gradients affect deep network training.
- [Deep Learning Libraries - TensorFlow, PyTorch & Keras](https://johnb.io/course/tensorflow-pytorch-keras): Practical comparison of PyTorch, TensorFlow and Keras for research prototyping and production deep learning.
- [Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Keras](https://johnb.io/course/cnns-with-keras): Convolutional layers, pooling, feature maps and building image classification models with Keras.
- [RNNs, Transformers & Autoencoders](https://johnb.io/course/rnns-transformers-autoencoders): Sequence modelling from recurrent neural networks and LSTMs to self-attention transformers and autoencoders.

### Unit 7 - Generative AI & Practical Applications
- [Generative AI Models - VAEs, GANs & Diffusion](https://johnb.io/course/generative-ai-models): How Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), diffusion models and autoregressive LLMs generate content.
- [Prompt Engineering & AI Agents](https://johnb.io/course/prompt-engineering-ai-agents): System prompts, few-shot examples, structured outputs, tool calling and autonomous multi-step AI agent loops.
- [RAG, Fine-Tuning & Enterprise AI Strategy](https://johnb.io/course/rag-finetuning-enterprise-ai): When to use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with vector search versus fine-tuning weights for enterprise AI systems.

### Unit 8 - AI in Production
- [Introduction to MLOps - From notebook to production](https://johnb.io/course/intro-to-mlops): Bridging the gap between Jupyter notebook experiments and reproducible, monitored production machine learning systems.
- [Model Deployment - APIs, containers & cloud services](https://johnb.io/course/model-deployment): Serving machine learning models via REST APIs, batch inference vs real-time endpoints, containerisation and latency trade-offs.
- [Monitoring & Drift - Keeping models healthy in the real world](https://johnb.io/course/monitoring-drift): Detecting data drift, concept drift and silent performance degradation in production ML and LLM pipelines.
- [CI/CD for ML - Automating the machine learning pipeline](https://johnb.io/course/cicd-for-ml): Automated testing, data validation, model registry versioning and continuous delivery pipelines for machine learning.

### Unit 9 - AI Strategy & Business Applications
- [How Organisations Adopt AI - The adoption journey & ROI frameworks](https://johnb.io/course/ai-adoption-journey): How organisations progress from ad-hoc AI pilots to governed, measurable production capabilities.
- [Build vs. Buy - Evaluating AI tools as a business](https://johnb.io/course/build-vs-buy): Framework for deciding when to buy commercial AI SaaS, integrate foundation model APIs, or train custom models.
- [AI Across Industries - Healthcare, marketing, finance & beyond](https://johnb.io/course/ai-across-industries): Where AI delivers measurable value across healthcare, finance, iGaming, retail, marketing and software engineering.
- [Making the Business Case for AI](https://johnb.io/course/business-case-for-ai): How to scope AI projects around specific bottlenecks, estimate token and infrastructure costs, and measure real ROI.

- [AI Models in 2026: What Actually Changed in the Last 12 Months](https://johnb.io/news/ai-models-2026) (17 August 2026, 10 min read) - Twelve months of AI, from the Sora shutdown to Claude Opus 5. What changed, what got cheaper, and what the evidence says about productivity.

- [GEO: A Practical Guide to Generative Engine Optimisation in 2026](https://johnb.io/news/geo-generative-engine-optimisation) (13 April 2026, 7 min read) - Generative engine optimisation explained: how GEO differs from SEO, what AI systems look for in content, whether llms.txt works, and what to actually do about it.
- [Claude Code VSC: AI Coding for Beginners](https://johnb.io/news/claude-code-vsc) (3 April 2026, 8 min read) - Claude Code VSC is Anthropic's AI coding assistant built into Visual Studio Code. What it does, how to install it, what it costs, and what to try first - for beginners with no technical background.

## Free AI & Machine Learning Course (9 Units, 35 Lessons)

- Unit 1: [What is AI? - History, definitions & the Turing Test](https://johnb.io/course/what-is-ai) (8 min) - Covers AI history from the 1950s Dartmouth Workshop, Alan Turing's 1950 test, AI winters, and why modern AI is pattern matching at scale.
- Unit 1: [Categories of AI - Narrow, General & Super AI](https://johnb.io/course/categories-of-ai) (6 min) - Explains the three tiers of AI capability: Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI), Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), and Artificial Superintelligence (ASI).
- Unit 1: [How AI Learns - Supervised, Unsupervised & Reinforcement Learning](https://johnb.io/course/how-ai-learns) (10 min) - The three core learning paradigms that power modern AI systems, with practical examples of labelled training, clustering and reward-driven agents.
- Unit 1: [AI vs. Augmented Intelligence](https://johnb.io/course/ai-vs-augmented-intelligence) (5 min) - Explores the practical distinction between autonomous AI replacing human tasks and augmented intelligence enhancing human judgment.
- Unit 2: [Traditional AI vs. Generative AI - Architecture differences](https://johnb.io/course/traditional-vs-generative-ai) (9 min) - How rules-based and predictive statistical AI differs from modern generative foundation models that synthesise text, code, audio and images.
- Unit 2: [Machine Learning, Deep Learning & Neural Networks - How they relate](https://johnb.io/course/ml-deep-learning-neural-networks) (10 min) - How classical machine learning, multi-layer neural networks and deep learning fit together and when simpler models outperform deep networks.
- Unit 2: [Key AI Subfields - NLP, Computer Vision & Edge AI](https://johnb.io/course/key-ai-subfields) (8 min) - Overview of natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, speech recognition, robotics and recommender systems.
- Unit 2: [AI Tools & Platforms - LLMs, Agents, RAG & the 2026 market](https://johnb.io/course/ai-tools-platforms-2026) (10 min) - Survey of the leading foundation models, APIs, cloud ML platforms and developer tools used in production in 2026.
- Unit 3: [Real-World AI Failures & Why Ethics Matter](https://johnb.io/course/ai-failures-ethics) (9 min) - Real-world case studies of AI deployment failures and the ethical governance principles needed to prevent harm.
- Unit 3: [Hallucinations, Bias & Intellectual Property](https://johnb.io/course/ai-hallucinations-bias-ip) (8 min) - Why large language models hallucinate, how training data bias propagates into decisions, and copyright and intellectual property considerations.
- Unit 3: [AI Governance Frameworks & Enterprise Guidelines](https://johnb.io/course/ai-governance-frameworks) (10 min) - How organisations and regulators govern AI systems under the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and UK AI principles.
- Unit 4: [Python Essentials for AI - Variables, data structures & control flow](https://johnb.io/course/python-essentials-for-ai) (12 min) - Core Python data structures, functions, comprehensions and environment management required for machine learning workflows.
- Unit 4: [Data Analysis with NumPy & Pandas](https://johnb.io/course/numpy-pandas) (12 min) - Vectorised array operations in NumPy and tabular data cleaning, filtering and aggregation with Pandas.
- Unit 5: [Linear Regression & Gradient Descent](https://johnb.io/course/linear-regression-gradient-descent) (11 min) - How linear regression models continuous outcomes and how gradient descent iteratively minimises a loss function.
- Unit 5: [Logistic Regression & Classification](https://johnb.io/course/logistic-regression-classification) (10 min) - Binary and multi-class classification using the sigmoid function, log-loss optimisation and decision thresholds.
- Unit 5: [Model Evaluation - Validation, Overfitting & Metrics](https://johnb.io/course/model-evaluation) (11 min) - Measuring model performance with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, ROC-AUC and cross-validation.
- Unit 5: [Key ML Algorithms - Decision Trees, SVMs & More](https://johnb.io/course/key-ml-algorithms) (12 min) - Decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, support vector machines (SVMs) and k-nearest neighbours compared.
- Unit 6: [Biological vs. Artificial Neurons](https://johnb.io/course/biological-vs-artificial-neurons) (7 min) - How biological neurons inspired the mathematical perceptron, weights, biases and activation thresholds.
- Unit 6: [Artificial Neural Networks & Forward Propagation](https://johnb.io/course/neural-networks-forward-propagation) (9 min) - How input features flow through input, hidden and output layers via matrix multiplication and non-linear activations.
- Unit 6: [Backpropagation & How Neural Networks Learn](https://johnb.io/course/backpropagation) (11 min) - How neural networks learn by applying the chain rule of calculus to propagate error gradients backward through layers.
- Unit 6: [Activation Functions & the Vanishing Gradient Problem](https://johnb.io/course/activation-functions-vanishing-gradient) (9 min) - ReLU, sigmoid, tanh and softmax compared, and how vanishing or exploding gradients affect deep network training.
- Unit 6: [Deep Learning Libraries - TensorFlow, PyTorch & Keras](https://johnb.io/course/tensorflow-pytorch-keras) (10 min) - Practical comparison of PyTorch, TensorFlow and Keras for research prototyping and production deep learning.
- Unit 6: [Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Keras](https://johnb.io/course/cnns-with-keras) (12 min) - Convolutional layers, pooling, feature maps and building image classification models with Keras.
- Unit 6: [RNNs, Transformers & Autoencoders](https://johnb.io/course/rnns-transformers-autoencoders) (13 min) - Sequence modelling from recurrent neural networks and LSTMs to self-attention transformers and autoencoders.
- Unit 7: [Generative AI Models - VAEs, GANs & Diffusion](https://johnb.io/course/generative-ai-models) (11 min) - How Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), diffusion models and autoregressive LLMs generate content.
- Unit 7: [Prompt Engineering & AI Agents](https://johnb.io/course/prompt-engineering-ai-agents) (10 min) - System prompts, few-shot examples, structured outputs, tool calling and autonomous multi-step AI agent loops.
- Unit 7: [RAG, Fine-Tuning & Enterprise AI Strategy](https://johnb.io/course/rag-finetuning-enterprise-ai) (11 min) - When to use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with vector search versus fine-tuning weights for enterprise AI systems.
- Unit 8: [Introduction to MLOps - From notebook to production](https://johnb.io/course/intro-to-mlops) (10 min) - Bridging the gap between Jupyter notebook experiments and reproducible, monitored production machine learning systems.
- Unit 8: [Model Deployment - APIs, containers & cloud services](https://johnb.io/course/model-deployment) (11 min) - Serving machine learning models via REST APIs, batch inference vs real-time endpoints, containerisation and latency trade-offs.
- Unit 8: [Monitoring & Drift - Keeping models healthy in the real world](https://johnb.io/course/monitoring-drift) (9 min) - Detecting data drift, concept drift and silent performance degradation in production ML and LLM pipelines.
- Unit 8: [CI/CD for ML - Automating the machine learning pipeline](https://johnb.io/course/cicd-for-ml) (10 min) - Automated testing, data validation, model registry versioning and continuous delivery pipelines for machine learning.
- Unit 9: [How Organisations Adopt AI - The adoption journey & ROI frameworks](https://johnb.io/course/ai-adoption-journey) (10 min) - How organisations progress from ad-hoc AI pilots to governed, measurable production capabilities.
- Unit 9: [Build vs. Buy - Evaluating AI tools as a business](https://johnb.io/course/build-vs-buy) (8 min) - Framework for deciding when to buy commercial AI SaaS, integrate foundation model APIs, or train custom models.
- Unit 9: [AI Across Industries - Healthcare, marketing, finance & beyond](https://johnb.io/course/ai-across-industries) (10 min) - Where AI delivers measurable value across healthcare, finance, iGaming, retail, marketing and software engineering.
- Unit 9: [Making the Business Case for AI](https://johnb.io/course/business-case-for-ai) (9 min) - How to scope AI projects around specific bottlenecks, estimate token and infrastructure costs, and measure real ROI.

## Who is John Bowman?

John Bowman is an AI strategist and developer based in Leeds, UK. I've spent more than 20 years in iGaming and digital marketing, and I now design, build and ship AI tools under my own name at [JohnB.io](https://johnb.io/).

**Term:** AI strategist. **Definition:** someone who works out where AI belongs in a business and where it doesn't, then proves it by building the thing rather than presenting a slide about it.

The career underneath that is unglamorous and specific. Multilingual poker and casino operations across 40 countries. Fraud investigations. Over £150k recovered in chargebacks. Live event media. Then digital and SEO leadership across 24 language markets, and product ownership of cross-functional teams above 90 people with £1.5M+ of budget attached.

## What do I build at JohnB.io?

Free tools, mostly. More than 20 of them are live and none ask you to sign up: the [T&Cs Simplifier](https://johnb.io/tcs-simplifier), the [iGaming Compliance Map](https://johnb.io/igaming-compliance), the [LLMs.txt Generator](https://johnb.io/llms-generator), an [AI Copyeditor](https://johnb.io/editor), and a free 35-lesson [AI and Machine Learning course](https://johnb.io/course/) with a certificate at the end.

Every one is a static HTML page plus a Cloudflare Worker that holds the API key and the rate limit. No framework, no build step, no package manager. That's a deliberate choice and I'd defend it: a page that loads in under a second and still works when JavaScript fails is worth more than the same tool wrapped in 400kb of React.

That principle got tested on this page. The skills panels above used to be generated by JavaScript, which meant every AI crawler that reads the site without running scripts saw six unlabelled buttons and nothing else. They're rendered in the HTML now.

## Why does 20 years in iGaming matter for AI work?

Because iGaming is one of the few industries where a bad automated decision comes with a regulator attached. Send the wrong bonus message to a self-excluded customer and it isn't a bug, it's a fine.

So the questions I ask about any AI deployment come in a fixed order: what happens when the model gets it wrong, who signs it off, and what the audit trail looks like. That's why I built the [AI Governance Framework](https://johnb.io/rai) and the compliance map before I built anything more interesting.

The failure I see most often is a company buying an LLM licence and calling it a strategy. Most of the value sits in the dull part around the model: who reviews the output, what gets logged, which decisions a human still has to make. Nobody wants to hear that in a kick-off meeting.

## What did 88 million AI music views actually pay?

£600. Between 2024 and early 2026 I made 60 AI-generated tracks, distributed them through SoundON Global, and they picked up 88 million views. Nine of them passed a million each. The total payout was six hundred pounds.

I keep coming back to that number because it's the cleanest lesson in AI economics I've had first hand, and it complicates the point I made earlier about building things yourself. Generating output is now nearly free. Distribution isn't, and reach and revenue stopped being the same measurement somewhere around 2024. The full write-up is here: [what happens when your AI songs get 88 million views](https://johnb.io/news/ai-music-88-million-views).

## Where did John Bowman train in AI?

The **University of Oxford AI Programme in 2024** is the qualification that matters most, followed by IBM Generative AI Engineering in 2026. Before either of those: a Professional Diploma from the Digital Marketing Institute in 2016, New Technologies for Business Leaders at Rutgers University in 2020, and a run of CalArts UI/UX courses through 2021.

More recent additions are DataCamp's Responsible AI Practices and Understanding the EU AI Act, both completed in 2026. The full dated list sits in the Education panel above.

Certificates don't make anyone an engineer, and I'd say that with a long list of them sitting right above this paragraph. They're a record of finishing things. Useful, and not the same as being able to ship.

## What do I write about?

Practical AI: how it behaves rather than how a vendor deck says it behaves. Recent pieces cover [generative engine optimisation](https://johnb.io/news/geo-generative-engine-optimisation), what genuinely changed in [AI models over the last 12 months](https://johnb.io/news/ai-models-2026), and the free [35-lesson AI and machine learning course](https://johnb.io/course/) that explains the terminology properly for people tired of nodding along.

I don't publish to a schedule. Pieces go up when I've got something I'd want to read myself, which means three in a month and then nothing until August.

# Privacy Policy

> How JohnB.io handles analytics, AI tool inputs, registered course accounts, cookies, and UK GDPR data protection rights.

- **Canonical URL**: https://johnb.io/privacy
- **Markdown URL**: https://johnb.io/privacy.md
- **Author**: [John Bowman](https://johnb.io/about)
- **Last Updated**: 6 April 2026

> **Disclosure:** UK GDPR Data & Privacy Rights: Requests for data access, correction, deletion, or portability can be submitted via https://johnb.io/contact and are handled within 30 days.

Legal

Last updated: 6 April 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how JohnB.io collects, uses, and protects your personal data. JohnB.io is operated by John Bowman, United Kingdom. We take your privacy seriously and comply with the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018.

## 1. Data controller

The data controller is John Bowman, trading as JohnB.io. Contact via the [contact form](https://johnb.io/contact).

## 2. What data we collect

### Account users (registered)

When you create an account, we collect:

- Your name and email address
- Authentication method (email/password or Google sign-in)
- Course progress data (which lessons you have completed)
- Exam results (score, grade, date)
- Account creation date
- Newsletter consent preference and the date consent was given (if opted in)

### All visitors

We collect anonymised usage data via Google Analytics, including:

- Pages visited and time spent
- Device type, browser, and approximate location (country/city)
- Referral source

This data does not identify you personally.

### AI tool inputs

When you use AI-powered tools on the Site, your input text is sent to third-party AI APIs (such as Anthropic) to generate a response. We do not store your input text beyond what is needed to process the request. Please do not submit personal, sensitive, or confidential information into AI tools.

## 3. How we use your data

We use your data to:

- Provide and operate your account
- Track and display your course progress
- Issue your course certificate upon completion
- Send you updates about new lessons and content, if you have opted in
- Improve the Site based on aggregated analytics
- Respond to support enquiries

We do not use your data for advertising, and we do not sell your data to third parties.

## 3a. Newsletter and marketing emails

When you create an account, you may choose to opt in to occasional updates about new lessons and content. This is entirely optional — the tick box is unchecked by default.

We will only send you marketing emails if you explicitly checked the opt-in box at signup. If you signed up via Google or GitHub, the same applies: consent is only recorded if the box was checked on the signup panel at the time of account creation.

Every marketing email includes an unsubscribe link. You can also withdraw consent at any time via the [contact form](https://johnb.io/contact) and we will stop sending within 5 working days.

The legal basis for sending marketing emails is your consent (UK GDPR Article 6(1)(a)). We log the date and time of your consent alongside your account data.

## 3b. Affiliate disclosures

JohnB.io participates in affiliate programmes for certain products and services mentioned on the Site. This means that if you click an affiliate link and make a purchase, JohnB.io may receive a small commission at no extra cost to you. Affiliate income does not influence editorial coverage or tool recommendations; resources featured on JohnB.io are chosen on merit and usefulness to our audience.

## 4. Legal basis for processing

- **Contract:** Processing your name and email to provide account services
- **Legitimate interests:** Improving the Site using anonymised analytics
- **Consent:** Where you have opted in to any communications

## 5. Data storage and security

Account data is stored securely in Google Firebase (Firestore), hosted on Google Cloud infrastructure. Google Firebase is compliant with GDPR and ISO 27001. We implement appropriate technical measures to protect your data, including encrypted connections (HTTPS) and Firebase security rules that restrict access to your own data only.

No system is completely secure. We cannot guarantee the absolute security of your data but we take reasonable steps to protect it.

## 6. Third-party services

The Site uses the following third-party services that may process your data:

- **Google Firebase** — authentication and database (Google LLC, USA). Governed by Google's Privacy Policy and the Google Cloud Data Processing Addendum.
- **Google Analytics** — anonymised usage tracking (Google LLC, USA)
- **Anthropic / OpenAI / other AI APIs** — processing of text inputs submitted to AI tools
- **Stripe** — payment processing for paid tools and subscriptions (Stripe Inc., USA). Your payment data is processed by Stripe and is subject to their [Privacy Policy](https://stripe.com/gb/privacy).
- **Cloudflare** — infrastructure and security (Cloudflare Inc., USA)
- **Namecheap** — web hosting (Namecheap Inc., USA)

International transfers to the USA are covered by Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent safeguards.

## 7. How long we keep your data

- **Account data:** Retained for as long as your account is active. Deleted within 30 days of an account deletion request.
- **Analytics data:** Retained by Google Analytics per their standard retention settings (26 months).
- **AI tool inputs:** Not stored beyond immediate request processing.

## 8. Your rights under UK GDPR

You have the right to:

- **Access** — request a copy of the personal data we hold about you
- **Rectification** — ask us to correct inaccurate data
- **Erasure** — request deletion of your account and personal data
- **Restriction** — ask us to limit how we process your data
- **Portability** — receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format
- **Object** — object to processing based on legitimate interests

To exercise any of these rights, use the [contact form](https://johnb.io/contact) and select "Data / privacy request". We will respond within 30 days.

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the UK's supervisory authority: the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at [ico.org.uk](https://ico.org.uk).

## 9. Cookies

The Site uses cookies for the following purposes:

- **Authentication:** Firebase uses session cookies to keep you logged in
- **Analytics:** Google Analytics uses cookies to track anonymised usage

You can disable cookies in your browser settings, though this may affect Site functionality including staying logged in.

## 10. Children's privacy

The Site is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 13. If you believe a child has created an account, please contact us and we will delete the account promptly.

## 11. Changes to this policy

We may update this policy from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Significant changes will be notified via a notice on the Site.

## 12. Contact

For any privacy-related questions or requests: [contact form](https://johnb.io/contact).

# Search & Prompt Radar

> Free keyword and prompt research tool that pulls live autocomplete suggestions from Google Search and YouTube, Reddit search intent, recent Hacker News threads and LinkedIn B2B modifiers, then synthesises likely ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude prompts using Claude Haiku 5.5.

- **Canonical URL**: https://johnb.io/search-radar
- **Markdown URL**: https://johnb.io/search-radar.md
- **Author**: [John Bowman](https://johnb.io/about)
- **Last Updated**: October 2026

> **Disclosure:** AI assistant prompts shown in Search & Prompt Radar are not taken from ChatGPT logs (no AI platform publishes prompt logs); they are synthesised by Claude Haiku 5.5 from live Google, YouTube, Reddit and Hacker News search demand.

## Autocomplete Is the Most Honest Free Demand Signal

Google, YouTube and Reddit only suggest a phrase when enough real people type it. That makes autocomplete the most honest free signal of demand you can get. Paid keyword tools estimate volume from samples and clickstream panels. Autocomplete shows you the actual wording, including the awkward questions nobody would put in a content brief. If you're writing for [FAQ schema](https://johnb.io/faq-schema) or an [llms.txt file](https://johnb.io/llms-generator), that wording is what you want.

The AI prompts card is different, and I'd rather say so up front. No AI platform publishes its prompt logs: not OpenAI, not Anthropic, not Google. So those prompts are synthesised, not scraped. An AI model reads the real search data collected here and writes the prompts people are most likely asking ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity about the same topic. If that step fails, you get rule-based prompts instead and the badge says so. Use them to shape AEO and GEO content, and don't report them to anyone as measured demand.

## How It Works

1. **Enter a seed.** A product, tool, problem or topic between 2 and 80 characters, such as n8n automation.
2. **Pick a region.** UK, US or Global. It changes the country hint sent to Google and YouTube.
3. **Scan.** The tool queries Google autocomplete, YouTube autocomplete and Hacker News in parallel, then shows which platforms answered and which didn't.
4. **Synthesise prompts.** The collected terms go to an AI model, which writes likely assistant prompts and groups the terms into intent clusters. If that step fails you get rule-based prompts, labelled as such.
5. **Filter and copy.** Narrow the results to Questions, Comparisons or Tutorials, and click any term, prompt or hook to copy it.
6. **Export.** Copy everything as Markdown to paste into an LLM, or download a CSV for a spreadsheet. The page URL updates too, so you can share the scan.

## Key Points

- **Autocomplete reflects real typing.** A suggestion only appears when enough people search the phrase, so it's evidence of demand rather than a model's guess.
- **Questions are your FAQ and PAA targets.** The question group in the Google card is the closest free proxy for People Also Ask boxes. Answer them in 40 to 60 words directly under the heading.
- **Comparisons signal buying intent.** People searching "vs" and "alternative" are close to a decision. These pages convert better than broad explainers.
- **Tutorial searches show what people want shown, not told.** If a YouTube query has thin results, a written guide with screenshots can take that traffic too.
- **Discussion threads give you the frustrated wording.** Hacker News and Reddit thread titles often make better H2s than anything a keyword tool suggests, because they're how people describe the problem.
- **AI prompts are estimates.** They're built from the search data, not from AI platform logs. Good for shaping AEO and GEO content, wrong for reporting demand. Run them through the [Prompt Improver](https://johnb.io/prompt-improver) if you want to test them yourself.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Search & Prompt Radar free?

Yes. It's free and there's no sign-up. Each IP address gets 20 fresh scans a day, and repeating a scan that's already cached doesn't count towards that limit.

### Where does the data come from?

Google and YouTube autocomplete suggestions for your seed, Reddit search suggestions from Google, and Hacker News threads from the last 12 months. The LinkedIn card turns that demand into B2B angles, and the AI prompts card is synthesised from all of it. A repeat scan of the same seed can return a cached copy rather than fresh data.

### Are the ChatGPT prompts real?

They're not taken from ChatGPT. No AI platform publishes its prompt logs, so the prompts are synthesised from the real Google, YouTube, Reddit and Hacker News data the tool collects. Treat them as a reasoned estimate of what people ask AI assistants, grouped by Discovery, Comparison and Implementation intent.

### Why does the tool show Hacker News threads instead of Reddit threads?

Reddit now blocks anonymous access to its search data, so live Reddit threads can't be fetched without an approved API account. The tool still shows what people search for on Reddit, taken from Google autocomplete, and links straight to Reddit search. Live threads come from Hacker News, which works best for tech, AI and startup topics.

### Can I export the results?

Yes. Copy all for LLM copies every result as clean Markdown you can paste into ChatGPT, Claude or a content brief. Export CSV downloads a file with platform, category and term columns that opens in Excel or Google Sheets. You can also click any single term to copy it.

### What does the region setting change?

It sets the country Google and YouTube use for their suggestions, so UK returns British phrasing and spelling while US returns American queries. Global drops the country hint altogether. Hacker News is one site worldwide, so its threads don't change between regions.

## Sources & Primary References

1. [Google Search Help - How Google autocomplete predictions work](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/7368877)
2. [YouTube - How YouTube search works](https://www.youtube.com/howyoutubeworks/product-features/search/)
3. [Reddit Help - Reddit Data API Wiki](https://support.reddithelp.com/hc/en-us/articles/16160319875092-Reddit-Data-API-Wiki)
4. [Algolia - Hacker News Search API](https://hn.algolia.com/api)
5. [Anthropic - Claude documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com)

# AI Meditation Generator

> Generates personalised guided meditations with Claude Sonnet 5.5 scripts, OpenAI TTS narration, and 10 browser-synthesised Web Audio soundscapes in 25 languages across 5, 10 or 20-minute sessions.

- **Canonical URL**: https://johnb.io/meditation
- **Markdown URL**: https://johnb.io/meditation.md
- **Author**: [John Bowman](https://johnb.io/about)
- **Last Updated**: July 2026

> **Disclosure:** This is a relaxation aid, not medical advice. Meditation is not a treatment for any medical condition, including high blood pressure, anxiety disorders or insomnia. If you have a health concern, speak to a doctor.

## Why a Generated Meditation Beats a Library

Meditation apps hand you a library of pre-recorded sessions and ask you to find one that fits. This tool works the other way round: you say what you want to work on, and the session is written for you on the spot. Your name appears in it. The pacing matches the length you chose. A sleep session slows down and lets you drift off; a focus session brings you back to a single point of attention.

The voice is generated by OpenAI text to speech, the script by Claude, and the soundscape is synthesised live in your browser with the Web Audio API - no recordings, no loops, no two sessions the same.

## How It Works

1. **Fill in the form.** Your first name is optional. Pick a goal or describe your own, choose 5, 10 or 20 minutes, then select a voice and a soundscape.
2. **Claude writes your script.** The AI writes a timed meditation built around your goal - short spoken passages with deliberate pauses between them, personalised with your name.
3. **The voice is generated.** Each passage is converted to speech by OpenAI text to speech at a slowed, calm pace. The first passage is ready within seconds; the rest load quietly in the background.
4. **Press play.** Your browser synthesises the soundscape live with the Web Audio API and plays each spoken passage at the right moment, gently lowering the music while the voice speaks.
5. **Follow the voice.** When the session ends the soundscape fades out slowly. Take a moment before you move. You can also download the finished session as an MP3, or share it straight to WhatsApp from your phone.

## Key Points

- **Consistency beats length.** Five minutes every day does more than twenty minutes once a week. Start with the 5-minute option and build up.
- **A wandering mind is the exercise.** Noticing you have drifted and coming back is not failing at meditation - it is the repetition that trains attention.
- **Posture matters less than stillness.** Sitting in a chair with both feet on the floor works fine. For sleep sessions, lie down in bed and let the session end without you.
- **Match the session to the moment.** Focus sessions work best before deep work, relaxation sessions after stress, sleep sessions as the last thing you do with the lights off.
- **Headphones change the experience.** The soundscape sits under the voice and the stereo detail is lost on laptop speakers.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What does the AI Meditation Generator do?

It creates a personalised guided meditation from three inputs: your name, what you want to work on and how long you have. Claude writes a script built around your goal, an AI voice reads it aloud, and a calming soundscape plays underneath. Every session is unique.

### Is it free?

Yes. You get 3 meditations per day at no cost. The limit exists because each session costs real money in AI usage. If you want more than 3 a day, get in touch on LinkedIn.

### Is this medical advice?

No. This is a relaxation aid, not a treatment for any medical condition, including high blood pressure, anxiety disorders or insomnia. If you have a health concern, speak to a doctor. Stop the session if you feel unwell.

### Do you store my name or goal?

No. Your name and goal are sent to a Cloudflare Worker, used to generate the script and audio, and never saved. The only thing stored is a rate-limit counter tied to your IP address, which expires within two days.

### Why does the voice pause between passages?

Guided meditation is mostly silence. The voice speaks for a few seconds, then leaves space for you to follow the instruction while the soundscape continues. Longer sessions use longer pauses, and sleep meditations use the longest of all.

### Can I listen with the screen locked?

Not reliably. The audio is generated and mixed live in your browser, and phones suspend browser audio when the screen locks. Keep the tab open and the screen on, or use a desktop. Headphones give the best experience.

### Can I download my meditation?

Yes. Once all the voice passages have loaded, use Download MP3 to save the full session with the voice and soundscape mixed at the background volume you set on the slider. On a phone, the Share button sends the file straight to WhatsApp or any other app.

## Sources & Primary References

1. [NHS - Mindfulness](https://www.nhs.uk/mental-health/self-help/tips-and-support/mindfulness/) - what mindfulness is and how it supports mental wellbeing.
2. [NHS - Breathing Exercises for Stress](https://www.nhs.uk/mental-health/self-help/guides-tools-and-activities/breathing-exercises-for-stress/) - the breathing techniques these sessions draw on.
3. [Goyal et al., JAMA Internal Medicine (2014)](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/fullarticle/1809754) - meta-analysis of meditation programmes and psychological wellbeing.
4. [Text to Speech tool](https://johnb.io/text-to-speech) - the same AI voices, for any text you like.

# Live Poker Hand Replayer

> Turn any live No Limit Hold'em poker hand into an animated table replay using a guided form or AI note parser powered by Claude Haiku 5.5, with optional OpenAI TTS commentary, share links and iframe embeds.

- **Canonical URL**: https://johnb.io/live-poker-hand-replayer
- **Markdown URL**: https://johnb.io/live-poker-hand-replayer.md
- **Author**: [John Bowman](https://johnb.io/about)

## How It Works

1. **Enter the hand.** Use the builder to set blinds, players, stacks and cards, then tap the action as it happened - the tool only ever offers legal moves. Or paste your written notes and let the AI build the hand for you.
2. **Watch the replay.** The hand plays out on the table: chips slide in, streets are dealt, stacks update. Step forward and back through every decision or let it auto-play at 1x, 1.5x or 2x.
3. **See the result.** At showdown the tool ranks the hands, names the winner ("two pair, kings and eights") and ships the pot - side pots and split pots included.
4. **Share it.** Copy a link that holds the entire hand, or grab the embed code and put the replay in a forum thread or on your own site.

## Key Points

- **Built for live hands.** No hand history files needed - if you can describe the hand, you can replay it.
- **Poker-correct.** Turn order, minimum raises, all-ins, side pots and split pots all follow the rules automatically.
- **Nothing stored.** The whole hand is compressed into the share link - no server, no database, no account.
- **Embeds anywhere.** The iframe embed works on forums, blogs and coaching sites.
- **2 to 9 players.** Heads-up to full ring, cash or tournament, with antes and straddles.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What does the Live Poker Hand Replayer do?

It turns a poker hand you describe into an animated replay on a virtual table. You see every player's name, chip stack and position, then step through each bet, call, raise and fold street by street, right up to the showdown.

### Is the Live Poker Hand Replayer free?

Yes. Building hands with the form, replaying, sharing and embedding are free with no limits. The AI note parser is also free but capped at 5 hands per day to keep the tool running.

### Can I share a replay with friends?

Yes. Every replay gets a short share link that's easy to post anywhere, and anyone who opens it sees the same replay. You can also copy an embed code to drop the replay into a forum post, blog or website.

### What happens if the AI can't read my notes?

You never lose your work. Whatever the AI did manage to understand is loaded into the hand builder form, with a note on what's missing, so you fill in the gaps rather than starting again.

### Which poker games does it support?

No Limit Hold'em with 2 to 9 players, as a cash game or a tournament hand. Antes and straddles are supported, and all-ins with side pots are worked out automatically.

### Do you store my hands anywhere?

Only the hand itself, never anything about you. Short links keep the hand's details behind a random code so they stay tiny, while embed codes carry the whole hand inside themselves. There are no accounts, and hands are never linked to who made them.

## Sources & Primary References

1. [Poker TDA Rules — the tournament rules this tool's betting logic follows](https://www.pokertda.com/poker-tda-rules/)
2. [List of poker hands — standard hand rankings used at showdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_poker_hands)
3. [Side pots — how all-in pots are split among players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betting_in_poker#Side_pots)
4. [Bankroll Calculator](https://johnb.io/bankroll) - related poker tool on this site.

# AI CV Enhancer

> Upload a CV (PDF, DOCX or TXT) and job description to get a tailored CV, cover letter, suitability match score and interview prep powered by Claude Sonnet 5.5 in 9 language variants, plus integrated job board search.

- **Canonical URL**: https://johnb.io/aitocv
- **Markdown URL**: https://johnb.io/aitocv.md
- **Author**: [John Bowman](https://johnb.io/about)
- **Last Updated**: October 2026

> **Disclosure:** Privacy Notice: JohnB.io does not log, store or share the CV or job description content you submit. Inputs are processed ephemerally via Anthropic's API.

The AI CV Enhancer takes your existing CV and a job description, then produces a tailored CV, a matching cover letter, a suitability score and a set of interview prep questions - all in under 60 seconds. It is designed for job seekers who want to move fast without sacrificing quality. The tool also includes a role-fit finder that analyses your CV and suggests the ten job titles you are best suited for, plus a searchable directory of job boards for the UK, Italy, Spain, France, Brazil, Portugal, Romania, Germany, Malta and Bulgaria, alongside iGaming and gambling recruiters and international and remote boards. The domain [aitocv.com](https://aitocv.com) redirects here.

The tool runs on [Claude Sonnet by Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude), a more capable model chosen for the complexity of tailoring professional documents to specific roles. Your CV and job description are sent securely to Anthropic's API and are not stored or used to train AI models. The tool complies with [UK GDPR](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/) and the [Anthropic Privacy Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy) as of March 2026. Always review the output before sending to employers - do not include sensitive personal information such as passport numbers or financial details.

## How It Works

1. **Upload your CV.** by dropping a PDF, DOCX or TXT file onto the upload area, or paste the text directly into the input field below it.
2. **Paste the job description.** into the right-hand panel. The more detail the job listing includes - responsibilities, required skills, company context - the more precisely the tool can tailor your CV. Leave the output language on Same as the job description, or pick one of nine languages.
3. **Click Enhance My CV & Write Cover Letter.** Claude Sonnet analyses both documents, rewrites your CV to highlight the most relevant experience, and generates a personalised cover letter for the role.
4. **Review your results.** You will receive a tailored CV, a cover letter, a suitability score out of 10, a list of any skills gaps to address, and a set of likely interview questions with suggested answers.
5. **Download your documents.** as Word or PDF files. Use the role-fit finder to discover other roles that suit your background, and the job board search to apply directly.

## Key Points

- **ATS-optimised output.** The tailored CV is structured to pass [Applicant Tracking Systems](https://www.jobscan.co/applicant-tracking-systems) used by most large employers. Keywords from the job description are incorporated naturally rather than stuffed artificially.
- **Cover letter included.** Rather than a generic template, the cover letter is written using your real background and the specific role requirements. It reads as a genuine application, not filler.
- **Suitability score and skills gap analysis.** A match score out of 10 shows how well your CV aligns with the role, alongside a clear list of any skills or experience the employer is asking for that your CV does not currently demonstrate.
- **Interview preparation included.** The tool generates likely interview questions based on the job description and your CV, along with suggested answers drawn from your own experience - useful for preparation without starting from scratch.
- **Role-fit finder.** Not sure what jobs to apply for? Upload your CV and click Find My Best Roles - Claude will return your top ten best-fit job titles based on your skills and experience.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Which AI model does this tool use?

The tool uses [Claude Sonnet by Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude) - specifically Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`). Sonnet is a more capable model than Claude Haiku and was chosen here because tailoring professional documents to specific roles requires stronger reasoning and instruction-following than simpler tasks.

### Is my CV stored or shared?

No. Your CV and job description are sent to Anthropic's API to process your request only. Anthropic does not use API inputs to train its models by default, and JohnB.io does not log, store or share the content you submit. See the [Anthropic Privacy Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy) for full details. Do not include highly sensitive personal information such as passport numbers, national insurance numbers or financial details.

### What file formats can I upload?

The tool accepts PDF, DOCX and TXT files. PDF and DOCX are recommended for preserving formatting. The text content is extracted on upload - embedded images and complex tables may not transfer perfectly, so check the extracted text before submitting.

### Can it write my CV in another language?

Yes. Choose an output language under the job description: English, Italian, Spanish, French, Portuguese (Brazil or Portugal), Romanian, German or Bulgarian. The default, Same as the job description, matches the language the job advert is written in, so a Spanish advert gets a Spanish CV, cover letter and interview prep. Company names and qualification titles are kept as they are, and the PDF download supports accented letters and Cyrillic.

### How good is the tailored CV at beating ATS screening?

The output is designed to incorporate relevant keywords from the job description in a natural way, which improves ATS pass rates. However, every employer configures their ATS differently. Tools like [Jobscan](https://www.jobscan.co) can give you a more precise match score for a specific ATS. Use the AI output as a strong starting point, then review it yourself before applying.

### What is the daily usage limit?

The tool allows up to 20 enhancements per day per user. This limit applies per IP address and resets at midnight UTC. If you need higher-volume access, [get in touch via LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-bowman/).

# AI Copyeditor

> Paste or upload text and Word documents for AI-powered copyediting powered by Claude Sonnet 5.5 with UK/US English support, custom brand style guide rules and excluded words.

- **Canonical URL**: https://johnb.io/editor
- **Markdown URL**: https://johnb.io/editor.md
- **Author**: [John Bowman](https://johnb.io/about)
- **Last Updated**: March 2026

The AI Copyeditor reviews and improves your writing - fixing grammar, tightening sentences, adjusting tone and enforcing consistent style. Paste any article or upload a .txt, .doc or .docx file, configure your preferences in the Advanced Options, and click Analyse Article. Results appear in seconds.

The tool runs on [Claude Sonnet 5.5 by Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/sonnet). Your text is sent securely to Anthropic's API for processing and is not stored or used to train AI models. The tool complies with [UK GDPR](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/) and the [Anthropic Privacy Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy) as of March 2026. Always review the output before publishing - treat it as a strong second draft, not a final one.

## How It Works

1. **Paste your article.** into the text area, or click *Choose File* to upload a .txt, .doc or .docx file directly.
2. **Optionally expand Advanced Options.** to set your preferred language (UK or US English), writing style (Conversational, Professional, Persuasive and more), a brand style guide, any words or characters to exclude, and a target article length.
3. **Click Analyse Article.** Your text is sent to Claude Sonnet 5.5, which copyedits it according to your settings.
4. **Review the results.** The edited article appears in the Results section. Compare it with your original and accept or discard individual changes as you see fit.
5. **Download your edited article.** as a TXT or DOCX file, ready to paste into your CMS or share with a client.

## Key Points

- **UK and US English supported.** Switch between British and American spelling and punctuation conventions in Advanced Options - useful if you publish for different regional audiences.
- **Ten writing styles available.** From Conversational and Persuasive to Analytical and Narrative - the tool adapts tone and structure to match your goal rather than imposing a single house style.
- **Brand style guide input.** Paste your own style guidelines into the Advanced Options and the tool will respect them during editing. Useful for maintaining consistent brand voice at scale.
- **Handles long-form content.** The tool accepts full-length articles. Use the article length selector to target a specific word count or summarise longer pieces.
- **Export-ready output.** Download edited articles as TXT or DOCX with one click - no copy-paste formatting issues.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What does the AI Copyeditor actually change in my text?

It corrects grammar and spelling, improves sentence clarity, adjusts tone to match your chosen writing style, and restructures awkward phrasing. It does not fact-check or add new information. The output is your article improved, not rewritten from scratch.

### Which AI model does this tool use?

The tool uses [Claude Sonnet by Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/sonnet) - specifically the `claude-sonnet-5-5` model. Anthropic is an AI safety company and Claude is their primary language model family, designed to follow detailed instructions reliably.

### Is my text stored or used to train the AI?

No. Your text is sent to Anthropic's API to process your request and is not retained or used for training. See the [Anthropic Privacy Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy) for full details. JohnB.io does not log or store the content you submit.

### What file types can I upload?

The tool accepts .txt, .doc and .docx files. Word documents (.docx) are recommended for best formatting fidelity. The text content of your document is extracted on upload - embedded images and tables are not processed.

### Will the edited article pass AI detection tools?

Not reliably. If the AI rewrites significant portions of your text, those sections may be flagged by detectors such as [GPTZero](https://gptzero.me) or [Originality.ai](https://originality.ai). Review the output and rewrite anything that does not sound like you before publishing.

# Gen Z Translator

> AI-powered translator using Claude Haiku 5.5 that rewrites plain English into Gen Z slang and translates Gen Z slang back into plain English.

- **Canonical URL**: https://johnb.io/genz
- **Markdown URL**: https://johnb.io/genz.md
- **Author**: [John Bowman](https://johnb.io/about)
- **Last Updated**: March 2026

The Gen Z Translator converts standard English into Gen Z slang - or decodes Gen Z text back into plain English. Paste any sentence, paragraph or document and hit Translate. You can also swap the direction using the arrow button, so it works both ways. It is built for marketers, teachers, curious parents, or anyone who wants a laugh.

The tool runs on [Claude Haiku by Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/haiku). Your input is sent securely to Anthropic's API and is not stored or used to train AI models. The tool complies with [UK GDPR](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/) and the [Anthropic Privacy Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy) as of March 2026. Results are intended for entertainment - not all slang will be current or appropriate for every context.

## How It Works

1. **Type or paste your text.** into the left panel. You can also upload a .txt, .doc or .docx file using the Choose File button.
2. **Check the translation direction.** By default the tool translates from English to Gen Z. Click the swap button between the two panels to reverse the direction - useful for decoding Gen Z text into standard English.
3. **Click Translate.** Your text is sent to Claude Haiku, which rewrites it in the target style using current Gen Z vocabulary and phrasing patterns.
4. **Read the result.** in the right panel. The output preserves the meaning of your original text while changing the register and vocabulary.
5. **Copy or share the result.** directly from the output panel, or run it through again with the direction swapped to check the translation back.

## Key Points

- **Two-way translation.** Translate English into Gen Z slang or convert Gen Z text back into standard English - the swap button switches direction instantly.
- **Useful for marketers and educators.** Brands targeting younger audiences use it to sanity-check campaign copy. Teachers use it to decode messages or create relatable examples for students.
- **AI-driven, not dictionary-driven.** Because the tool uses a language model rather than a fixed word-swap list, the output reads naturally in context rather than producing awkward literal substitutions.
- **Built for fun, not formal use.** The disclaimer is on the page for a reason - results can be unpredictable and slang evolves quickly. Always review the output before using it professionally.
- **No account needed.** Free to use with a daily per-IP limit to keep it available for everyone. Resets at midnight UTC.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Which AI model powers this tool?

The tool uses [Claude Haiku by Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/haiku) - specifically the `claude-haiku-5-5` model. It is a fast, lightweight model that is well-suited to short-form style transformation tasks like this one.

### How accurate is the Gen Z slang?

Claude is trained on large amounts of real online text, so results are generally natural and contextually appropriate. That said, slang evolves quickly and regional variations exist. Some outputs may feel slightly dated or miss nuance. The tool is a starting point, not a guarantee of authenticity.

### Can I use this for marketing content?

You can use it to generate ideas or check tone, but always have someone from your target audience review the output before publishing. Misused slang can land badly. The tool is most useful as a creative prompt or research aid rather than a production pipeline.

### Is my text stored or used to train the AI?

No. Your input is sent to Anthropic's API solely to process the translation request and is not retained or used for training. See the [Anthropic Privacy Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy) for full details. JohnB.io does not log or store the content you submit.

### Why is there a disclaimer about offensive content?

Gen Z slang includes terms that can carry different meanings depending on context, community or tone. The tool is designed to be fun and educational, not offensive. If a result feels inappropriate for your audience, discard it - the AI is not always aware of every cultural nuance.

# LLM Chat

> Side-by-side chat interface comparing Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT and Google Gemini responses to the same prompt in real time.

- **Canonical URL**: https://johnb.io/lm-chat
- **Markdown URL**: https://johnb.io/lm-chat.md
- **Author**: [John Bowman](https://johnb.io/about)
- **Last Updated**: March 2026

LLM Chat runs three AI models side by side - [Claude Sonnet by Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude), [GPT-4o-mini by OpenAI](https://openai.com/gpt-4o-mini), and [Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite by Google](https://deepmind.google/technologies/gemini/flash/). You can chat with each model individually or use the broadcast bar to send the same prompt to all three simultaneously and compare the responses in real time. It is useful for evaluating which model handles a specific task best, stress-testing prompts across providers, or simply exploring how different models approach the same question.

Each model maintains its own conversation history within the session, so you can have multi-turn conversations with each one independently. Prompts are routed securely through a [Cloudflare Worker](https://workers.cloudflare.com) proxy to the respective provider APIs. Your messages are subject to the privacy policies of each provider: [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy), [OpenAI](https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy), and [Google](https://policies.google.com/privacy). Do not include sensitive personal information in your prompts.

## How It Works

1. **Chat with one model.** Type a message in the input box under any of the three panels (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini) and press Enter or the send button. The model responds in that panel. Each panel maintains its own conversation thread, so you can continue a multi-turn dialogue with any one model independently.
2. **Broadcast to all three.** Type a prompt in the broadcast bar at the top and click Send to All. The same message is sent to all three models simultaneously and responses appear side by side, making it easy to compare how each model handles the same prompt.
3. **Compare responses.** Look across the three panels to see differences in tone, accuracy, length and reasoning. This is particularly useful for tasks like summarisation, creative writing, code generation or answering complex questions where model behaviour varies noticeably.
4. **Continue the conversation.** After a broadcast, you can follow up with each model individually. Each panel remembers its own prior turns, so you can dig deeper into a specific model's response without affecting the others.
5. **Clear and reset.** Use the delete button in the broadcast bar to clear all three conversations and start fresh.

## Key Points

- **Three leading models, one interface.** Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Anthropic), GPT-4o-mini (OpenAI) and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite (Google) - all in a single view. No switching between tabs or platforms.
- **Broadcast mode saves time.** Send the same prompt to all three models at once and see responses arrive in parallel. Useful for prompt engineering, benchmarking or demos.
- **Multi-turn conversations supported.** Each panel maintains full conversation history for the session, so you can have extended back-and-forth exchanges rather than one-shot queries.
- **Routed via a secure proxy.** API keys are never exposed in the browser. All requests go through a Cloudflare Worker, keeping credentials server-side.
- **Good for prompt engineering and model evaluation.** If you are developing prompts for a production system and need to decide which model to use, this tool gives you a quick side-by-side view without writing any code.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Which AI models are used?

The tool connects to three models: `claude-sonnet-5-5` by [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com), `gpt-4o-mini` by [OpenAI](https://openai.com), and `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` by [Google DeepMind](https://deepmind.google). These are current production models as of August 2026.

### Are my messages stored?

Conversation history exists only in your browser for the current session and is cleared when you close the tab. Prompts are forwarded to each provider's API - they are subject to the respective privacy policies of [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy), [OpenAI](https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy) and [Google](https://policies.google.com/privacy). JohnB.io does not log or retain your messages.

### Why use GPT-4o-mini rather than GPT-4o?

GPT-4o-mini is a cost-efficient model that performs well for most conversational and reasoning tasks, making it a practical choice for a free comparison tool. For tasks requiring maximum capability from OpenAI, GPT-4o or GPT-o1 would be more appropriate - but those are better evaluated via [ChatGPT](https://chat.openai.com) directly.

### Can I use this to decide which model to use for my project?

Yes - this is one of the best use cases. Run your specific prompts through all three models and compare quality, speed and tone. Keep in mind that model performance varies by task type: coding, creative writing, factual Q&A and structured reasoning can produce noticeably different results across providers.

### Is there a usage limit?

There is no hard limit on the tool itself, but the underlying APIs have rate limits managed at the Cloudflare Worker level. If you hit a limit, wait a moment and try again. For high-volume testing, the best approach is to access the provider APIs directly with your own keys.

- **Canonical URL**: https://johnb.io/text-to-speech
- **Markdown URL**: https://johnb.io/text-to-speech.md

This tool converts text to natural-sounding speech using the OpenAI TTS API and lets you download the result as an MP3 file. It is built for content creators, publishers, bloggers and anyone who wants to add audio to written content without recording it manually. Choose from six AI voices, adjust the playback speed, and download the finished file in seconds.

The tool uses OpenAI's tts-1 model. Your text is sent securely to OpenAI's API for processing and is not stored or used for training. There is a daily usage limit per IP address to keep the tool free and available for all users.

## How It Works

1. **Choose your voice and speed.** Six voices are available: Alloy (neutral), Echo (male), Fable (British male), Onyx (deep male), Nova (female) and Shimmer (soft female). Speed ranges from 0.75x to 1.5x normal pace.
2. **Paste or type your text.** Up to 4,000 characters per conversion. For longer content, split it into sections and convert each one separately.
3. **Click Convert to Speech.** The tool sends your text to OpenAI's TTS API, which generates an MP3 audio file. This typically takes 2 to 5 seconds depending on text length.
4. **Preview and download.** The audio player appears once generation is complete. Use the player to preview, then click Download MP3 to save the file to your device.

## Key Points

- **Powered by OpenAI TTS.** This tool uses the tts-1 model from OpenAI, which produces natural-sounding speech without robotic artefacts. It is the same model used in ChatGPT voice mode.
- **Six voice options.** Each voice has a distinct character. Nova and Shimmer suit narration and editorial content. Onyx works well for podcasts and deep-read formats. Fable has a British English cadence suited to formal content.
